newsitem.title: ITALY: LIFFE studying possibility of modifying contracts.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE studying possibility of modifying contracts.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) is considering whether to modify specifications of contracts on all government securities but has not made any decisions, a LIFFE official said on Tuesday.

Giuliano Gregorio, director of LIFFE's Business Development Interest Rate Products, told Reuters by telephone from London changes in contracts depended on how European economic and monetary union (EMU) progresses and on the needs of LIFFE members.
"At the moment nearly all our members are convinced that with the arrival of EMU, we shouldn't make changes that could show themselves to be inadequate shortly afterwards," he said.
"The less one touches the specifications the better," he added.
Italian financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported recently LIFFE wanted to halve the nominal coupon on the BTP futures contract to six from 12 percent.
"LIFFE, which monitors the market constantly, has no plan for an immediate change in specifications and much less to halve coupons. The Btp is not first on the waiting list," Gregorio said.
"Certainly the contract above 130 is a sign of a wide difference between market rates and the nominal coupon but there are precedents relative to other contracts," he said.
Currently the benchmark 10-year Btp is yielding about 7.5 percent, much less than its nominal 12 percent coupon.

"We are monitoring all coupons on government securities but before we take a decision, a medium-term analysis will be made. The recent doubts on EMU have made traders more lukewarm about reductions on coupons," Gregorio said.
From a technical point of view the first Btp future which could change is the December contract, which is already listed but which no one has yet started to trade.

"The general principle is not to modify contracts which are already listed, unless there are urgent factors which push us into being more flexible. In that case the one necessary condition is that there are no open positions on it," he said.

Traders say rollover from the front month contract to the next one usually starts about a month before the front contract expires. Traders have different opinions on the gap between market rates and the nominal coupon on the future.
"Anyone who plays the curve and trades basis is happy. Other people would like the difference to be reduced," one said.

Gregorio said the final date for taking decisions on the future structure of government securities futures contracts was June 1998 when March 1999 contracts would be listed. These will be the first contracts following the projected start of a European single currency on January 1, 1999.
